record.paper_title: FPT Suspects and Tough Customers: Open Problems of Downey and Fellows
record.original_question: Given a k-polymatroid M, is there a fixed-parameter algorithm in k that decides whether M is hypergraphic, meaning that M is the hypergraphic polymatroid of some hypergraph?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A k-polymatroid is a pair (E, r) where E is a finite ground set and r : 2^E → ℤ_{≥0} is a function (the rank function) satisfying: (i) r(∅) = 0; (ii) r(X) ≤ r(Y) whenever X ⊆ Y ⊆ E (monotonicity); (iii) r(X ∪ Y) + r(X ∩ Y) ≤ r(X) + r(Y) for all X, Y ⊆ E (submodularity); and (iv) r({e}) ≤ k for every e ∈ E. Given a hypergraph H = (V, E), the hypergraphic polymatroid of H is the polymatroid on the edge set E whose rank function r_H assigns to each subset F ⊆ E the value |V(F)| − c(F), where V(F) is the set of vertices incident to some edge in F and c(F) is the number of connected components of the sub-hypergraph (V(F), F). A k-polymatroid M is called hypergraphic if M is isomorphic to the hypergraphic polymatroid of some hypergraph.

Assume that M is given by an oracle access to its rank function (or by an explicit listing of values). The problem is the following.

Does there exist an algorithm that, on input a k-polymatroid M on n elements, decides whether M is hypergraphic in time f(k) · n^{O(1)} for some computable function f depending only on k? In other words, is the parameterized problem of recognizing hypergraphic k-polymatroids, parameterized by k, fixed-parameter tractable?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of recognizing hypergraphic k-polymatroids is listed as open in surveys of parameterized complexity. Related polynomial-time results exist for verifying whether a polymatroid arises from a specific given hypergraph (work of Vertigan–Whittle and related authors), but no FPT algorithm in k for the general recognition problem appears in the literature; the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Recognizing Polymatroids Associated with Hypergraphs
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm decides in polynomial time whether a polymatroid is the hypergraphic polymatroid associated with a given hypergraph.
status_evidence.claim: Related polynomial-time recognition results exist but the parameterized version in k of general hypergraphic-polymatroid recognition is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Shortest paths on polymatroids and hypergraphic polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Subsequent work on hypergraphic polymatroids; does not resolve FPT recognition.
status_evidence.claim: No FPT algorithm for hypergraphic k-polymatroid recognition is reported.
